messages:
maria: Quick thread to align on soft-eviction + burst telemetry requirements for Dedicated GA. I sketched an MVP launch checklist and some non-negotiables. Need eng + ops buy-in before this week's roadmap meeting.

kenji: Ack. Can you paste the checklist?

maria: Sure — high level:
- MVP features: reserved pool admission, soft-eviction pathway, short burst windows (5m), burst accounting ledger, basic tenant-facing quota dashboard.
- Telemetry: per-tenant p95 latency, burst-usage time series, prewarm credit consumption, eviction events + reason codes, backlog queue length.
- Autoscale policy: primary trigger = sustained queue length > threshold for 60s, fallback = token-rate delta > 2x baseline for 30s.
- Launch criteria: latency SLOs met in canary (p95 < 500ms for gen workloads), no silent-data-loss on eviction, docs + self-serve conf in console.

sarah: Adding constraints from runtime: we need kernel warmup latency baked in. If we do 5m burst windows, the KV cache cold start will add ~80-120ms p95 for first N tokens unless we prewarm. That affects the p95 SLO for canary slices.

kenji: Right. Two operational asks: telemetry retention for burst histograms should be 30d for debugging; and we need an aggregated daily snapshot exported to billing for chargeback.

ralph: Ops note: soft-eviction must emit an event with tenant_id, pool_id, reason_code, active_requests, and fallback_model. Ops-bot: please add template.

ops-bot: /event-schema registered: soft_eviction_v1 {tenant_id, pool_id, ts, reason_code, active_requests:int, fallback_model, prewarm_credit_used:float} :white_check_mark:

maria: Nice. A few policy questions: 1) Should bursts be contiguous 5m windows (user-facing), or allow fragmented bursts (internal ledger)? 2) Do we allow carryover of unused burst credits between billing cycles for pilots?

product_lead: For GA MVP we should keep it simple: contiguous windows, no carryover. Pilot customers can opt-in to carryover via contract.

kenji: Implementation note: contiguous windows are easier for admission and simpler for cache eviction heuristics. But they mean stricter denial periods. We'll need to tune soft-eviction gracebands.

sarah: Proposed soft-eviction graceband algorithm: proportional-fade — when pool pressure > 90% start soft-evicting tenants proportional to recent burst usage weighted by SLA tier. Eviction sequence emits a 'soft_eviction_warning' 30s before deny, with estimated time to retry.

maria: Good. Add acceptance criteria: warnings are sent and visible in tenant dashboard within 5s of decision; denied requests get 429 + structured payload with fallback_model.

ralph: Also require an ops escape hatch: manual override that can lift soft-eviction for a pool for up to 15 minutes with audit log.

product_lead: Docs + support playbook must include clear messaging for customers about behavior during soft-eviction, recommended retry backoffs, and best-effort fallbacks.

kenji: Telemetry specifics — can we standardize names and labels? Suggest: metric names: dedicated.burst_usage{tenant,pool}, dedicated.queue_length{pool}, dedicated.latency_p95{tenant,pool}, dedicated.evictions_count{tenant,pool,reason}. Export via OTLP.

ops-bot: Telemetry schema note: ensure cardinality limits: max 10k unique tenant labels per cluster, otherwise metrics will be sampled.

sarah: For autoscale triggers we need a canary plan: roll to 5% reserved pool traffic, measure p95, evictions, and autoscale oscillation. Canary duration: 48 hours with a 4-hour baseline window.

maria: Launch checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Admissions + contiguous burst windows implemented (eng)
- [ ] Soft-eviction + warning events (eng + ops)
- [ ] Telemetry pipeline + retention + billing export (obs/infra)
- [ ] Console UI: burst usage + warnings (devex)
- [ ] Support playbook + customer message templates (cs + marketing)
- [ ] Canary plan + acceptance tests (sre/product)

kenji: Owners? I can own telemetry pipeline. Sarah can own autoscale + runtime changes. Maria you own product acceptance and docs. Ralph owns ops escape hatch and alerting.

maria: Perfect. Can we get target dates? Propose end-of-sprint (2 weeks) for feature flags + canary gating, and GA cut 6 weeks if canary passes.

product_lead: Timeline OK but add contingency: if canary shows >5% increase in p95 for top 10 tenants, pause and do rollback.

ralph: Alert rules: fire P1 if evictions_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m on any pool on GA traffic. Also P2 if telemetry export fails >5m.

kenji: Small config snippet for autoscale trigger (proposal):
```
autoscale:
  queue_threshold: 250
  sustained_window: 60s
  token_rate_multiplier: 2.0
  cooldown: 120s
```

sarah: We'll prototype that and add hysteresis to prevent thrash: require 3 consecutive windows before scale up/down.

maria: Final asks before I add to roadmap doc: confirm retention numbers (30d burst hist, 90d lat percentiles?), and billing export format (CSV daily or BigQuery?).

kenji: 30d for histograms is fine. Lat percentiles 90d. Export to BigQuery is preferred (schema compatible), CSV fallback for small customers.

product_lead: OK. I'll add to roadmap doc: start canary next Tuesday, owners as discussed, contingency and accept criteria baked in.

maria: Thanks all — I'll post PR with the checklist and add the policy text for proportional-fade. If anyone has objections, flag here today. :thumbsup:
